<explanation>
1. Project Type and Purpose
   - This is an open-source, full-stack Android application (“Androidify”) demonstrating AI-driven avatar creation. It uses Jetpack Compose for UI, CameraX for camera features, Firebase AI Logic SDK (Gemini API) for image/text generation, and Navigation 3 for Compose navigation. The code is highly modularized into Gradle modules to separate features and core services.

2. Key Architectural Components
   a. App Module (app)
      - Entry point for the Android application.
      - Hosts the AndroidifyApplication (Application subclass), MainActivity, and configures Navigation.
      - Depends on feature modules, core modules (network, util, theme), and data modules.
   b. Feature Modules (feature/home, feature/camera, feature/creation, feature/results)
      - Each provides a Compose screen, ViewModel (MVVM), UI components, and tests.
      - Expose navigation routes and interact with shared data services via interfaces in “data” module.
   c. Data Module (data)
      - Defines repositories (ImageGenerationRepository, TextGenerationRepository) and data sources.
      - Provides Retrofit/network abstractions and connectivity management.
      - Supplies DI (DataModule) for ViewModels across features.
   d. Core Modules
      - core/network: Network clients, Firebase initializers, RemoteConfigDataSource, Vertex AI data source, DI (NetworkModule).
      - core/theme: Shared Compose theming, custom brushes, transitions.
      - core/util: Utility classes (file provider, graphics, layout, animation helpers).
      - core/testing: Test runners, fake data sources, repository fakes for unit/integration tests.
   e. External Services
      - Firebase (App Check, Remote Config, AI Logic SDK).
      - Vertex AI / Imagen and Gemini models via FirebaseAiDataSource.
   f. Benchmark Module (benchmark)
      - Contains performance and startup benchmarks for the app’s AI and UI flows.

3. Relationships and Data Flow
   - UI Layer (Compose Screens in feature modules) ← ViewModels (feature/*.ViewModel) ← Repositories (data module) ← DataSources (core/network).
   - Navigation component coordinates between feature screens via MainNavigation.
   - NetworkModule (Hilt or manual DI) provides singletons for Retrofit, Firebase, RemoteConfig.
   - DataModule provides repository implementations to ViewModels.
   - CameraX component (feature/camera) interacts with CameraProvider and feeds bitmaps to the ImageGenerationRepository.
   - Generated images/text pass back from the AI service through repositories to the ViewModel, then rendered in a Compose UI screen (feature/results).
   - Remote Config can alter endpoints or feature toggles at runtime.

4. Architectural Patterns and Design Principles
   - MVVM: Each screen has a ViewModel that exposes UI state and events.
   - Modularization: Separate Gradle modules per feature and core capability for compile-time isolation and faster build times.
   - Dependency Injection: NetworkModule and DataModule supply singletons and interfaces for testability.
   - Clean Separation: UI vs. business logic vs. data sources vs. external services.
   - Compose Navigation Graph: Defined in MainNavigation, decoupled per feature.

5. Diagram Construction Guidelines
   - Use layers (or horizontal swimlanes):
     • Presentation Layer: feature/home, feature/camera, feature/creation, feature/results.
     • Domain/Data Layer: data module (repositories).
     • Infrastructure Layer: core/network (Firebase, Vertex AI), core/util.
     • App Host: app module (Application, Activity, Navigation).
     • External Systems: Firebase services, Vertex/Imagen API.
   - Draw arrows to show:
     • UI event → ViewModel method calls.
     • ViewModel → Repository interface.
     • Repository → Network/Data source.
     • Network/Data source → Firebase/Vertex API.
     • Firebase Remote Config → Network configuration at startup.
   - Highlight important technologies next to components:
     • Jetpack Compose in feature modules.
     • CameraX in feature/camera.
     • Firebase AI Logic SDK in core/network.
     • Navigation 3 in app/MainNavigation.
   - Color-code or shape-code each type:
     • Feature modules (e.g., blue rectangles).
     • Core services (green).
     • Data layer (yellow).
     • External systems (gray clouds).

6. Tailoring to This Android Project
   - Emphasize Compose UI modules on the left, flowing rightward to data and network modules, ending in external services.
   - Show modular Gradle boundaries and how each feature depends on core and data modules.
   - Include the benchmark module separately, linking to core/network and app module.
   - Note the role of core/testing in providing fakes for unit tests (dotted lines).

7. Diagram Elements Checklist
   - Clearly label each module (app, feature/*, data, core/*, benchmark).
   - Use directional arrows for data/control flow.
   - Group modules by layer and annotate DI modules (NetworkModule, DataModule).
   - Represent Firebase services (App Check, Remote Config, AI Logic) as external clouds.
   - Apply consistent shapes (e.g., rectangles for modules, cylinders for repositories/databases, clouds for external services).
   - Add a legend explaining color/shape conventions.

By following these guidelines, you’ll produce a detailed, accurate system design diagram that captures Androidify’s modular structure, MVVM patterns, and integration with Firebase-backed AI services. 
</explanation>
